newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Up to 14 EMU members by 2001 - CS Holding.
newsitem.headline: Up to 14 EMU members by 2001 - CS Holding.

text.p: There is a 70 percent chance that as many as 14 countries -- including Europe's southern tier -- could join Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) by 2001, CS Holding analysts forecast on Friday.

"If EMU comes about in 1999, a broad interpretation of the convergence criteria will be necessary. A start with the Deutschemark-bloc, France, Ireland and perhaps Finland would then be possible," they said in a report.

It pointed out that EU members would decide by qualified majority in early 1998 whether to launch the single currency, adding: "This will not work without the votes of Italy, Spain, Portugal and Sweden."

To coax them to support EMU with only core countries as members at first, the EU would have to grant these countries concessions. This could entail binding their currencies to the Euro in an intervention band.

These countries would also surely be promised that they could join EMU by 2001 if they met the convergence criteria by then, the report said, adding that this seemed realistic assuming narrowing interest rate differentials and acceptable economic growth.
"Thus EMU could consist of 14 countries in 2001 if Britain and Denmark decide to join. We put the probability that this scenario will take place at 70 percent."

The report by Joseph Scherrer and Rainer Marian forecast that demand for Swiss francs would remain strong in the run-up to EMU and that Swiss interest rates would remain low given slow economic growth and an improved outlook for inflation.

It cut its forecast for the yield on 10-year Swiss bonds to 4.0-4.5 percent in September 1997 from the previous 4.7-5.0 percent, and raised the 12-month target for the SMI blue-chip share index to 3,900 points from 3,700.
It suggested investors favour multinational companies like Novartis, Roche, Swiss Re, ABB, Adecco and SGS and underweight firms primarily engaged in domestic business.
